qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Proposals (RFP) issued by the City/County Association of Governments of San Mateo County for a planning project, containing a clear scope of work, submission deadlines, evaluation criteria, and budget information, all hallmarks of a procurement opportunity.

quotes.quote: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS San Mateo Countywide Safe Streets for All Supplemental Planning Project
Proposals are due: January 23, 2026, 12:00PM PST
To be considered for this work, proposers must submit a proposal in accordance with the requirements, specifications, and scope of work provided in this Request for Proposals (RFP).
C/CAG has budgeted four hundred thirty-three thousand, one hundred forty-one dollars ($433,171) for this effort.

findings.title: Project Scope and Available Budget
findings.fact: C/CAG is seeking qualified consultants for the San Mateo Countywide Safe Streets for All Supplemental Planning Project, funded through the SS4A Grant Program, with a budget of $433,171 and an anticipated contract term of approximately 48 months. The scope includes establishing a Transportation Safety Advisory Committee, plan monitoring and reporting, and an e-bike safety white paper.
findings.business_implication: Bidder can assess alignment with its capabilities and whether $433,171 is sufficient for the 4-year scope, including 16 quarterly TSAC meetings and 12 formal presentations.
findings.action_recommendation: Review Appendix A Scope of Work in detail, evaluate internal capacity, and prepare a pricing strategy within the stated budget.

quotes.quote: C/CAG has budgeted four hundred thirty-three thousand, one hundred forty-one dollars ($433,171) for this effort. C/CAG expects the work to commence on April 1, 2026 and to be completed no later than June 2030.
The anticipated contract term will be approximately 48 months.
Develop a comprehensive white paper to guide the County in establishing an effective and forward-looking electric bicycle (e-bike) policy and implementation approach.

findings.title: Minimum Qualification: Three Relevant Projects in Past Ten Years
findings.fact: Proposer must demonstrate to C/CAG's satisfaction that the prime consultant and/or one or more subconsultant proposed for this project have successfully completed at least three projects in the past ten years related to Local Roadway Safety Plan, Systemic Safety Analysis Report (SSAR), Vision Zero Action Plan and/or supplemental or implementation planning for the Safe Streets for All Grant Program.
findings.business_implication: Failure to demonstrate this will make the proposal nonresponsive and rejected. Teams must include at least one firm with qualifying project experience.
findings.action_recommendation: Gather documentation of three qualifying projects with dates and descriptions before submitting.

quotes.quote: Proposer must demonstrate to C/CAG’s satisfaction that the prime consultant and/or one or more subconsultant proposed this project have successfully completed at least three (3) projects in the past ten (10) years related to Local Roadway Safety Plan, Systemic Safety Analysis Report (SSAR), Vision Zero Action Plan and/or supplemental or implementation planning for the Safe Streets for All Grant Program.

findings.title: Minimum Qualification: Federal Grant Experience
findings.fact: Proposers must demonstrate experience managing and implementing large-scale federal grant funded projects and successfully ensuring compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements for such projects.
findings.business_implication: Teams must have proven federal compliance expertise; this may require adding a subconsultant with that background.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare examples of federal grant compliance and identify key personnel with this experience.

quotes.quote: Proposers must demonstrate experience managing and implementing large-scale federal grant funded projects and successfully ensuring compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements for such projects.

findings.title: Proposal Deadline and Submission Method
findings.fact: Proposals must be received by 12 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026, emailed with subject line 'RFP – San Mateo Countywide Safe Streets for All Supplemental Planning Project' to Eva Gaye (egaye@smcgov.org). Late proposals may be considered nonresponsive.
findings.business_implication: Missed deadline or incorrect submission method can disqualify the proposal. Need robust delivery confirmation.
findings.action_recommendation: Submit well before deadline; confirm receipt with Eva Gaye; include exact subject line.

quotes.quote: Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026, in accordance with the instructions contained in the RFP. Proposals should be emailed with the subject line “RFP – San Mateo Countywide Safe Streets for All Supplemental Planning Project” to: Eva Gaye (egaye@smcgov.org).
Proposals received after the time and date specified above may be considered nonresponsive.

findings.title: Proposal Format, Page Limits, and Appendix Caps
findings.fact: Proposals must be a single PDF with sequentially numbered pages and a table of contents; the body is limited to 20 pages excluding cover letter, title page, TOC, resumes, relevant experience, and references; required appendices/forms are excluded unless otherwise specified. Supplemental materials are capped at 5 pages and additional proposal requirements at 10 pages. Unsigned or unauthorized signatures are nonresponsive.
findings.business_implication: Bidder must carefully track page counts and ensure all required sections and forms are included without exceeding the stated caps.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare a compliance matrix and page-count tracking table; ensure signatures are from authorized representatives.

quotes.quote: Consultants must submit one (1) electronic copy of the proposal in pdf format. Each page shall be 8.5” x 11” or 11” x 17”. Each page shall be sequentially numbered, and a table of contents shall be provided. Each submittal shall be no more than 20 pages, excluding cover letter, title page, table of contents, resumes of key staff members, relevant experience, and references. All required appendices and forms are excluded from the 20 page limit unless otherwise specified.

findings.title: Mandatory State and Federal Forms
findings.fact: The proposal must include a Conflict of Interest Statement, Levine Act disclosure, litigation disclosure, agreement exception statement, signed insurance acknowledgement, W-9 with original signature, and federal certifications for lobbying, debarment/suspension, and SF-LLL. Federal forms do not count toward the page limit.
findings.business_implication: Missing or incorrectly executed forms can make the proposal nonresponsive or unawardable.
findings.action_recommendation: Use a checklist to assemble all required forms using the latest versions; obtain original signatures for W-9 and insurance acknowledgement.

quotes.quote: Include a Conflict of Interest Statement disclosing any financial, business or other relationship with C/CAG that may have an impact upon the outcome of the contract.
Complete the form available at: https://ccag.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Appendix-3-CA-Levine-Act-Statement.pdf and include it in your submission.

Submit a signed acknowledgement, for proposer only, that the proposer agrees to provide the required certificates of insurance providing verification of the minimum insurance requirements listed in Appendix D, Sample Agreement Template (see Section 11), within ten days of C/CAG’s notice to firm that it is the successful Proposer.
Submit a W-9, Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification for the proposer only (containing original signature), available at http://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fw9.pdf.

Proposals must contain the following federal certifications or forms: (1) Certification Regarding Lobbying, (2) Certification Regarding Debarment, Suspension, Ineligibility, and Voluntary Exclusion—Lower Tier Covered Transactions, and (3) Disclosure of Lobbying Activities (SF-LLL) form. It is the responsibility of the consultants to use the latest version of the applicable forms when submitting proposals. The forms are available at https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/cfo/contractor_recip/grant_agreement_form.cfm. These forms will not count toward the page limit.

findings.fact: RFP released Dec 19 2025; clarification deadline Jan 9 2026; proposals due Jan 23 2026 at 12:00 PM PST; interviews week of Feb 16 2026; Board approval Mar 12 2026; Notice to Proceed Mar 16 2026.
findings.business_implication: Bidder has a short window for clarifications and must be prepared for possible interviews in February and project start in March/April 2026.
findings.action_recommendation: Submit all clarifications by Jan 9; monitor C/CAG website for addenda; reserve interview dates.

findings.title: Contract Term and E-Bike White Paper Deadline
findings.fact: Work is expected to commence April 1, 2026 and complete by no later than June 2030; total contract duration shall be four years; e-bike white paper deliverable must be completed and submitted for final approval no later than December 31, 2026.
findings.business_implication: Bidder must price and staff for a four-year engagement, with an early milestone in the first nine months for the e-bike white paper.
findings.action_recommendation: Incorporate the December 2026 milestone into the work plan and schedule; allocate sufficient resources early in the project.

quotes.quote: C/CAG expects the work to commence on April 1, 2026 and to be completed no later than June 2030.

The schedule shall be based on an anticipated project kick-off during the week of April 1, 2026, and shall demonstrate completion of all work no later than June 30, 2030. The total contract duration shall be four (4) years; however, the e-bike white paper deliverable shall be completed and submitted for final approval no later than December 31, 2026.

findings.title: Evaluation Criteria and Weighting
findings.fact: Proposals are scored on a 0-5 scale multiplied by assigned weights. Written criteria total 80 points: Organization 5, Staff/Firm Qualifications 20, Understanding 20, Approach 15, Cost Effectiveness 15, References 5, Conflict of Interest Pass/Fail. If interviews are held, Presentation 10 and Q&A 10 contribute to a total of 100 weighted points / 500 maximum score. C/CAG may award without interviews.
findings.business_implication: Technical qualifications and scope understanding are weighted heavily (40 points combined), cost is only 15; oral interviews may not be held, so the written proposal must be comprehensive.
findings.action_recommendation: Emphasize staff qualifications and project understanding in the written proposal; price competitively but do not underpric; prepare for possible interviews but do not rely on them.

The final maximum score for any proposal is five hundred (500) points.
C/CAG reserves the right to not convene oral interviews or discussions, and to make an award on the basis of initial proposals.

findings.title: Budget Cap and Cost Proposal Requirements
findings.fact: C/CAG has budgeted $433,171 for this effort. The cost proposal must use the Appendix C template and include personnel names, classifications, hourly rates, and all direct/indirect costs. Rates are firm for the initial contract term and annual escalation cannot exceed 3%. C/CAG may negotiate or reject unreasonable rates.
findings.business_implication: Pricing must fit within the stated budget and comply with the fully loaded rate definition; there is limited room for escalation.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare the cost proposal using the template; verify rates are fully loaded and within budget; consider the 3% escalation cap in multi-year pricing.

quotes.quote: C/CAG has budgeted four hundred thirty-three thousand, one hundred forty-one dollars ($433,171) for this effort.

Provide a detailed task-based cost proposal for the project using the Cost Proposal Template (Appendix C). The cost estimate shall include personnel names, classifications, hourly rates, and any other cost items necessary to perform each of the tasks listed in the Scope of Work. A total cost shall be summarized and presented. Rates shall include all qualifying direct and indirect costs (consistent with the provisions of the terms and conditions of the Grant Agreement (Appendix B); fully loaded hourly rate means an hourly rate that includes all applicable surcharges such as taxes, insurance and fringe benefits as well as indirect costs, overhead and profit allowance, and ordinary materials and supplies. Rates indicated shall be firm for the initial contract term and any annual rate escalation shall not exceed 3%. C/CAG reserves the right to negotiate with or to decline to enter into a contract with a proposer whose rates are unreasonable at C/CAG’s sole discretion.

findings.title: Public Records Act Waiver and Indemnity
findings.fact: All information submitted in response to the RFP is a public record without exception; submission constitutes a waiver of any claim of protection from disclosure; proposer consents to release without notice and agrees to indemnify and hold harmless C/CAG for release of such information.
findings.business_implication: Confidential or proprietary information may be publicly disclosed, and the proposer may be liable for claims arising from such disclosure. This is a significant financial and reputational risk.
findings.action_recommendation: Avoid including sensitive proprietary information in proposals; consult legal counsel about the waiver and indemnity; consider whether any information can be protected under an exception, but note the RFP states no exception.

quotes.quote: Be advised that any contract that eventually arises from this RFP is a public record in its entirety. Also, all information submitted in response to this RFP is itself a public record without exception. Submission of any materials in response to this RFP constitutes a waiver by the submitting party of any claim that the information is protected from disclosure. By submitting materials, (1) you consent to release of such materials by C/CAG if requested under the Public Records Act without further notice to you, and (2) you agree to indemnify and hold harmless C/CAG for release of such information.

findings.title: Termination Rights for Conflict of Interest
findings.fact: If a consultant discovers a conflict during execution, it must notify C/CAG Project Manager immediately. C/CAG may terminate the contract involving the conflict and obtain conflicted services elsewhere. Failure to notify may be grounds for termination for cause under Section 4 of Appendix D.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must maintain active conflict monitoring; a conflict discovered mid-project could lead to termination and loss of revenue.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement a conflict-of-interest tracking process; promptly report any potential conflicts to C/CAG.

quotes.quote: If a consultant discovers a conflict during the execution of an assigned task, the consultant must immediately notify the C/CAG Project Manager regarding the conflict(s) of interest. The C/CAG Project Manager may terminate the contract involving the conflict of interest and C/CAG may obtain the conflicted services in any way allowed by law. Failure by the consultant to notify C/CAG Project Manager may be grounds for termination of the contract for cause pursuant to Section 4, Termination, of the Contract Agreement Template, provided as Appendix D to this RFP.

findings.title: C/CAG May Use Proposal Ideas Without Contract
findings.fact: This RFP is not a commitment; C/CAG reserves the right to pursue any and/or all ideas generated by this request. Proposal development costs are not reimbursed.
findings.business_implication: C/CAG could incorporate concepts from a non-winning proposal into its own plans without compensation, reducing value of intellectual capital.
findings.action_recommendation: Limit disclosure of proprietary methodologies or innovations; focus the proposal on qualifications rather than unique confidential ideas.

quotes.quote: This RFP is not a commitment or contract of any kind. C/CAG reserves the right to pursue any and/or all ideas generated by this request. Costs for developing the proposals are entirely the responsibility of the proposer and will not be reimbursed.

findings.title: Key Personnel Commitment and Material Breach
findings.fact: Key staff should be committed to the project for its duration; any change in key personnel requires prior written approval; removal without consent may be considered a material breach of contract.
findings.business_implication: The selected consultant could be in breach if key personnel leave or are replaced without permission, creating contractual liability.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure proposed key personnel have long-term availability; include backup staffing plans and obtain written approval for any changes.

quotes.quote: Resumes shall show relevant experience for the project Scope of Work, as well as the length of employment with the consultant. Key members, especially the project manager, shall have significant demonstrated experience with this type of project, and ideally should be committed to stay with the project for its duration. Any change in key personnel on the project team is subject to prior written approval of C/CAG. Removal of any key personnel identified in the responses to the RFP without prior written consent of C/CAG may be considered a material breach of contract.

findings.title: Actual Contract Terms and Templates Only Available via External Links
findings.fact: Appendices B (Grant Agreement), C (Cost Proposal Template), and D (Sample Agreement Template) are referenced but their content is not included in the provided RFP pages. The RFP directs proposers to external URLs for these documents.
findings.business_implication: Bidder cannot assess federal grant conditions, insurance minimums, termination provisions, or the cost template from the RFP alone; these may contain binding terms and affect pricing.
findings.action_recommendation: Download and review all linked appendices as part of proposal preparation; if links are unavailable, request copies from C/CAG.

findings.title: Conflict: 10-Year Minimum Qualification vs 5-Year Project Examples
findings.fact: Minimum qualifications require three relevant projects in the past ten years, while proposal requirements require detailed descriptions of a minimum of three projects within the past five years.
findings.business_implication: A proposer with qualifying projects only older than five years could meet minimum qualifications but fail to provide acceptable project examples, affecting evaluation or responsiveness.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with C/CAG before the Q&A deadline; include at least three projects from the past five years if possible to satisfy both.

findings.title: Conflict: Reference Period for Proposal Content vs Evaluation
findings.fact: The proposal requirements ask for references for work completed within five years of RFP issuance, while the evaluation criteria ask for references from agencies consulted 'in the past three years.'
findings.business_implication: Bidder may not know which standard will be used; references selected to meet one may not satisfy the other and could affect scoring.
findings.action_recommendation: Provide references from both the past three and five years to cover both; request clarification from C/CAG.

quotes.quote: Provide three to five references (no more than five including references for subcontractors) and their contact information. References should be for work completed within five years of the date of the issuance of this RFP, and the contact person must be currently accessible via the contact information provided to be considered.
Provide as reference the names of at least three agencies you currently or have previously consulted for in the past three years.

findings.title: Conflict: 48-Month Term vs June 2030 Completion
findings.fact: The RFP states the anticipated contract term is approximately 48 months, but also states work will commence April 1, 2026 and be completed no later than June 2030; a separate schedule says total contract duration shall be four years and completion by June 30, 2030.
findings.business_implication: The actual performance period appears to be up to 51 months (April 2026 – June 2030), which could affect staffing, overhead, and pricing assumptions.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification on the exact contract period; prepare schedule and pricing through June 2030 as specified, and evaluate costs for an extended period if needed.

quotes.quote: The anticipated contract term will be approximately 48 months.
C/CAG expects the work to commence on April 1, 2026 and to be completed no later than June 2030.

The schedule shall be based on an anticipated project kick-off during the week of April 1, 2026, and shall demonstrate completion of all work no later than June 30, 2030. The total contract duration shall be four (4) years; however, the e-bike white paper deliverable shall be completed and submitted for final approval no later than December 31, 2026.

findings.title: Contract Award Subject to Board Approval and Execution
findings.fact: Any contract resulting from the RFP will not have force or effect until approved and fully executed by C/CAG. If the selected proposer fails to enter into a contract in a timely manner, C/CAG may reject the proposal and enter into a contract with the next highest scoring proposer.
findings.business_implication: Selection does not guarantee a contract; the bidder must be prepared to execute documents promptly and may lose the award if contract finalization is delayed.
findings.action_recommendation: Have legal and management review the contract template during the proposal stage to expedite execution after selection.

quotes.quote: Should this RFP result in recommendation for award of a contract, the contract will not have any force or effect until it is approved and fully executed by C/CAG.

If the selected proposer fails to enter into a contract with C/CAG in a timely manner as determined by C/CAG, C/CAG reserves the right to reject the proposal and enter into a contract with the next highest scoring proposer.
